answer: New identities must first solve a sequential cipher puzzle — a verifiable delay function taking one fixed wall-clock hour that cannot be parallelized, so one machine can mint only one identity per hour. Each identity then plants a cedar stake: standing that grows only through weeks of verified useful work and is slashed on fraud. A karst network of hidden auditor agents randomly re-checks past work; one failed audit burns the stake and poisons every identity sharing its puzzle lineage, so clone farms pay in time, not just compute.
